bullets.text: Ive's hardware and interface work made technology welcoming and raised expectations of everyday craft.
That achievement sets up the essay's claim that design's next center of gravity lies beneath surfaces.
The essay shifts design's focus from visual arrangement to model behavior, context, and policy.
Surface quality still matters, but influence over AI-mediated experience now requires technical fluency.

sections.label: From designing games to studying intelligence

bullets.text: Game design introduces Hassabis as a builder of responsive behavior and emergent systems, not merely artifacts.
His move into neuroscience and DeepMind frames interdisciplinary study as preparation for building intelligence.

sections.label: Move 37 as a new keynote moment

bullets.text: AlphaGo's Move 37 becomes the essay's emblem of machine creativity rather than brute calculation.
AlphaFold carries the argument from games to scientific impact, presented as learned intelligence rather than hardcoded behavior.
The closing defines design leadership by shaping intelligence and previews a closer look at its technical substrate.

notes.text: The opening praises Ive before displacing him. This makes the argument about a change in design's materials and locus of influence, not a claim that beauty or his achievements were mistakes.

The essay predicts disappearing surfaces yet explicitly retains a role for buttons and animation. Read the shift as a change in where consequential decisions sit, rather than a claim that presentation no longer matters.

The keynote analogy changes what counts as a design revelation: an unexpected move replaces a visible object. How would designers evaluate a system whose valuable behavior is not specified in advance?
Calling Hassabis a design leader broadens the category from a professional title to shaping possibility. What responsibilities toward people's experience should accompany that broader definition?
